title: The latest Android 17 QPR2 beta for Pixels has hit an unexpected roadblock (Updated: Fixed)
summary: Manual downloads are returning 404 errors days after the rollout.
body: TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 is available, but its official OTA download links appear to be broken. Pixel testers trying to manually download the update are being met with 404 errors. Google hasn’t explained the issue yet, but we’ve reached out for more information. Update, September 1, 2026 (10:00 AM ET): Google has informed us that the issue has been resolved. Users can now easily access the manual download page without any 404 errors. Original article, August 31, 2026 (04:29 AM ET): Google’s Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 rollout appeared to be going smoothly when it landed late last week. But for those who need to manually sideload it, the experience has been considerably less straightforward. Google’s official OTA download links now appear to be broken, returning a 404 error when users attempt to download the required files.

title: Take a look: Users are now getting Android’s convoluted sideloading process, and everyone hates it
summary: Android owners are getting Google's new sideloading process, and new screenshots give us an even closer look.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR At least one Android device owner has received the advanced flow for sideloading apps. The user shared screenshots outlining the process, covering the 24-hour wait and more. Fellow users expressed frustration with this change, while our own poll earlier this year also revealed widespread opposition. Google announced a couple of weeks ago that it had started rolling out its advanced flow for sideloading apps on Android devices. This controversial new process requires users to restart their phones and then wait 24 hours before they can sideload apps, and a user has shared screenshots of this new flow. Redditor Super-Ad8814 recently received the new sideloading flow on their unidentified Android device. A shared screenshot (see first image below) indeed shows that you need to confirm whether someone asked you to allow sideloading. This section also informs users that scammers often tell victims to sideload apps. Google’s fine print adds that government employees and legitimate business representatives will never ask you to enable sideloading.

title: Android Auto could soon get its own Quick Settings tiles, one toggle at a time
summary: Android Auto could soon make it easier to reach Settings options without digging through menus.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Google is testing Android-style Quick Settings in Android Auto. These Quick Settings tiles appear at the top of Android Auto notifications. They currently offer only a single control for DND, but we expect more to be added soon. Google has already made bold claims about a major Android Auto redesign and promised to deliver it by the end of the year. The refresh brings a borderless design that adapts better to a variety of screen shapes, widget support, and a media player that doesn’t hog more space than it needs. These changes make the Android Auto interface comparable to Apple’s CarPlay and are expected to roll out in batches through the end of the year. While we await the big redesign, Google is experimenting with smaller changes, including the new Android Auto icon it quietly switched to earlier today. Along with it, Google is also testing new Android Auto features, and we dug them up for you.

title: Dolly Parton Set for First-Ever U.K. No. 1 Single Following Posthumous Streaming Spike
summary: The country music icon passed away last week (Aug. 28) at 80 following a short battle with cancer.
body: Dolly Parton is on course for her first-ever No. 1 on the Official U.K. Singles Chart following a posthumous surge in streams for her signature hit “9 To 5.” Penned for the 1980 comedy film of the same name, the song stands as one of Parton’s most iconic and beloved numbers, and hit a new peak of No. 12 on last week’s chart (Aug. 28). Yet “9 to 5” is now striding towards the summit in the chart’s midweek update (Aug. 30), which would give the country music icon her maiden U.K. No. 1 single. In a press release, the Official Charts Company reports a 350% week-on-week increase in streams and sales. Parton is also set for a major presence elsewhere in the upper reaches of the U.K. chart. Having previously reached No. 7 upon release, “Jolene,” her 1973 classic, is currently tracking at No. 2, while Kenny Rogers collaboration “Islands in the Stream” is up to No. 6. Related Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80 Last Tuesday (Aug. 25), it was announced that Parton had died in Nashville at age 80 after a brief battle with cancer. title: Kacey Musgraves Covers ‘9 to 5’ During MSG Show, Says She’s ‘Never Gonna Be Over’ Losing Dolly Parton
summary: The singer was the latest star to pay musical tribute to the country legend who died last week at 80.
body: Kacey Musgraves paid tribute to Dolly Parton again at her Madison Square Garden show in New York on Monday night (Aug. 31) by getting spacey, as she does. The singer discussed how hard it is for her to believe that Parton, who died last week at age 80 following a brief battle with cancer, is not part of our universe anymore. Musgraves told the crowd that Parton was a “supernova of a person,” according to Rolling Stone , sharing with the crowd that the thing that gives her solace is that Parton’s “soul and her bones are literally part of this galaxy, this universe, the fabric of space and time. I definitely, for sure, I would not be able to stand up here and do what I do if I hadn’t been for Dolly Parton.” A few days earlier, the singer switched up the run order at TD Garden show in Boston on Friday (Aug. 28) to pay homage to Parton just days after the “I Will Always Love You” star’s death by bringing back her Golden Hour ballad “Rainbow” back into the set. After dedicating it to Dolly, she then dove into Parton’s 1977 Billboard Hot 100 No. 3 hit “Here You Come Again.” On Monday, Musgraves was at it again treat…

title: How Sam Fender & Olivia Dean’s ‘Rein Me In’ Became the U.K.’s Longest-Running No. 1 Single Ever
summary: The song now holds the all-time record for the longest-running U.K. No. 1 single.
body: Sam Fender ’s show at the London Stadium in June 2025 remains momentous for many reasons. It was the midway point of the rollout of his Mercury Prize-winning LP People Watching , and also his largest ever headline show. But perhaps the most consequential moment from it came midway through the set, album deep cut “Rein Me In” got an airing, with the show’s support act Olivia Dean , then a rising star, joining on vocals for a new verse. Now their careers — and that song — appear unstoppable. “Rein Me In” is in record-breaking territory on the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart. The track has earned 23 weeks at No. 1, and became the longest-running No. 1 single of the 21st century after 16, surpassing Drake’s “Hotline Bling.” It has now pulled clear of Frankie Laine’s “I Believe” in the all time rankings, which notched 18 weeks at the summit back in 1953, to become the longest-running U.K. No. 1 single ever. In February, it earned the BRIT Awards’ publicly voted song of the year prize, with Dean and Fender on hand to collect the prize in Manchester. Amid chart dominance in early May, Dean returned the favor by inviting Fender to give the son…

title: Google’s new Extreme Charging on the Pixel 11 Pro XL has a heat problem
summary: Is being 5 minutes faster really worth the higher temperatures?
body: Getting the new Pixel 11 Pro XL to fast charge as quickly as Google claims is no easy feat. First, you need to grab yourself a 45W USB PD PPS charger that supports 21V for this specific protocol. Not a hugely tall order, but it might require buying a new charger, even if you have a relatively new PPS model that only supports 11V. Secondly, there’s a new option to toggle Google’s Extreme Charging capability, which promises to shave up to five minutes off your charging needs, but you’ll need some good fortune to get it to work. In a classic Google move, Extreme Charging isn’t available right out of the box. I still haven’t figured out the exact spell required to spring into life. In my experience, the Extreme Charging settings option appeared after charging the Pixel 11 Pro XL from empty to full twice and then simply waiting for it to show up. In any case, with the feature finally unlocked, I’ve been able to test the pros and cons of the latest Pixel’s boosted charging capabilities.

title: The Galaxy S26 FE is the wrong Samsung phone to buy right now
summary: The S26 FE seems fine, but that's not enough.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority Not content with launching three foldables and a pair of smartwatches this summer, Samsung is rounding off its latest launch window with the Galaxy S26 FE . It’s hard to object to the idea behind the FE — the core of a premium Samsung phone experience with some bits trimmed off to make it easier on your bank account. And I am fairly sure that when the Galaxy S26 FE is reviewed, it will score well. But it’s still going to be a phone that’s hard to find a suitable buyer for, due to its unfortunate mix of features and pricing.

title: Apple’s first folding iPhone won’t kill Android foldables — it will save them
summary: Apple could finally make foldables cool.
body: We’re fast approaching a decade since the first commercially available foldable phones arrived — yes, I’m counting the hilariously bad Royole FlexPai. Yet, despite the strides we’ve made in the technology behind them, foldables as a category are stuck behind a proverbial wall. Everyone from Samsung to Google, Motorola, and a plethora of Chinese OEMs have spent years redesigning hinges, improving displays, and offering increasingly aggressive trade-in deals to spur take-up. Despite that, foldables still make up just 1.6% of global smartphone shipments.

title: Gemini Live’s latest upgrade makes talking across languages easier
summary: A small UI tweak brings a surprisingly useful new capability.
body: TL;DR Google is refining Gemini Live’s redesigned Android interface with another small UI change. A new live translation option is rolling out, letting Gemini translate conversations between languages in real time. The update appears to be a gradual server-side rollout, with some devices getting the refreshed UI before the translation feature arrives. For most of its existence, Gemini Live’s interface barely changed. That shifted in April when Google began testing a redesign that ditched the dedicated full-screen experience. Now, Google appears to be quietly refining that experience again, and the latest change could be much more useful than another visual refresh. A new “Turn on live translation” option appears to be rolling out to some users, enabling Gemini Live to translate conversations between languages in real time.

title: Google TV Streamer just got a 50% price hike, but here’s how you can get it at the older price
summary: The older price still exists at a few places — but only until current stocks last.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google has increased the price of its TV Streamer 4K by 50%. It pegs the increase to rising component costs. Along with the Streamer, Google is also hiking prices for certain models of the Nest Cam and doorbells. The Google TV Streamer 4K , launched in 2024, is one of the most capable devices for converting any screen or an older dumb LCD or plasma TV into a smart TV. The Streamer’s 4GB RAM provides ample headroom for the ad-ridden Google TV homepage to load and scroll very easily, while offering bragging rights for the quickest Google TV updates. However, that bigger-than-others RAM is now adding to Google’s manufacturing bills (thanks to AI-driven RAM and storage shortages), and it’s being passed on to consumers. Google’s streaming hardware, which was selling at a 25% discount back in July , is now seeing a sharp 50% price hike. With this change, the TV Streamer, launched in 2024, is now available for $149.99 — up from $99.99. The prices have already been updated at the Google Store and Best Buy, but Amazon and Walmart continue to sell remaining units at the older price.

title: PSA: Gemini can adjust system settings on any Pixel running Android 17
summary: Hey Google, make my phone be quiet.
body: TL;DR Pixel 11 debuted a Gemini feature called Device Help that can automatically adjust device settings based on text prompts. Device Help is available on all Pixel phones running Android 17, a Googler has clarified. The feature is also coming to more devices in the future. The Pixel 11 series debuted a new Gemini feature called Device Help . Device Help lets you tell Gemini what you want to accomplish on your phone, and the AI will return the relevant settings and even offer to make multiple changes for you in a single tap. Now, we’ve learned that the feature isn’t a Pixel 11 exclusive. Google’s Minhaz A V recently posted a video of Device Help in action on X . The clip shows Gemini surfacing a set of features to help make the phone “comfortable to use at night,” including dark mode and screen brightness settings. More interestingly, though, the tweet says that Device Help is available on any Pixel phone running Android 17, and that it’s coming to more devices in the future.

title: Pixel 11 owners say their phones are waking up without being touched
summary: The reports on Reddit suggest one gesture is way too sensitive on the latest Pixels.
body: TL;DR Pixel 11 owners report the Lift to check phone feature is waking their screens with very little movement. Some commenters say the feature seems noticeably more sensitive than it was on their older Pixels. Disabling Lift to check phone appears to be the only workaround to stop the issue right now. Now that the Pixel 11 series has only been out in the wild for a short time, the inevitable early quirks are starting to emerge. One of them appears to involve Google’s usually handy ‘Lift to check phone’ feature, with Pixel 11 Pro owners reporting that their screens are waking with barely any movement at all. A Reddit user raised the issue after noticing their new Pixel 11 Pro repeatedly waking while simply sitting on a table. After experimenting with the phone’s wake settings, they found that disabling the gesture stopped the behavior.

title: Satellite SOS just proved why it could be your phone’s most important feature
summary: Satellite connectivity reportedly helped one survivor reach rescuers during the deadly Nepal flooding disaster.
body: Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority TL;DR A survivor of the tragic Nepal flood disaster says satellite connectivity helped him contact rescuers after conventional networks went down. He was reportedly able to reach a helicopter and was evacuated from the disaster area. The case shows the potentially life-saving value of satellite features being adopted by major phone manufacturers. Satellite connectivity has gradually become a more familiar smartphone feature in recent years, offering a way to call for help when conventional networks aren’t available. The technology has now reportedly proved its worth during the tragic Tibet-Nepal flooding, with one survivor saying it helped him contact rescuers and escape to safety. As reported by PhoneArena , a survivor caught up in the disaster said he was able to maintain communication with the outside world via satellite connectivity on his HUAWEI Mate X5 after regular network service was lost. He later posted about his experience on the social media account of HUAWEI Executive Director Richard Yu.

title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 is selling so well, Samsung is borrowing parts from the future
summary: The company is reportedly using future component reserves to fill the gap.
body: TL;DR Galaxy Z Fold 8 demand is reportedly outpacing Samsung’s expectations. A Display Driver IC (DDI) shortage is now putting pressure on Fold 8 production. Samsung is tapping future DDI reserves to keep making current Fold 8 units. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra just became the best-selling Android phone globally in Q2 2026, while the regular Galaxy S26 also cracked the top 10. Now, Samsung has another phone that people apparently want more than it expected — so much so that the company is reportedly dipping into component stock reserved for future production to keep the Galaxy Z Fold 8 coming. According to ZDNet Korea , Samsung is running short of the Display Driver IC (DDI) used to control the pixels on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 OLED display. Samsung has reportedly increased its component orders after demand for the passport-style foldable exceeded expectations. But its DDI supplier, Taiwan’s United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC), has little room to ramp up production.

title: Pixel’s Now Playing is about to get its lost feature back, and we saw the proof
summary: Along with multi-user support, a sync functionality, and more.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google updated the Now Playing app with subtle interface tweaks. It’s also moving closer to restoring Now Playing notifications, which it removed earlier this year. We have spotted Now Playing’s upcoming support for secondary user accounts on Pixel devices. Beyond that, a sync feature for Now Playing history is in the works. Now Playing is a Pixel-exclusive feature with few haters, but Google managed to rile up users when it refashioned it as a separate app this March . The supposed upgrade broke key functionality for users, including the ability to sync tracks with third-party services like Last.fm. Now the app is getting a new update with certain functionality tweaks — and the bigger promise of getting lost features back.

title: There’s already another tri-fold phone on the market, and it’s not from Samsung

One of the biggest changes from the original Mate XT is the way the device folds: the new model uses an inward-folding mechanism that keeps the inner screen protected at all times. HUAWEI was the first to enter the segment with the Mate XT , followed by the Mate XTs. Samsung then launched its own version, dubbed the Galaxy Z TriFold , though it had a short sales run. If you’re itching to get your hands on a tri-fold, HUAWEI is now gearing up to launch its next-gen tri-fold phone, featuring a significantly revamped folding mechanism. title: New Android 17 QPR2 feature lets you peek inside your phone’s secure sandbox
summary: Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 introduces new Private Compute Core data logging controls inside Privacy Dashboard.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 adds a dedicated “Data logging” menu for Private Compute Core within Privacy Dashboard. Users can toggle logging between Limited (up to three days/100MB) and Detailed (up to 12 hours/100MB) tiers, download logs, or delete them. Google rolled out Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 , and alongside several under-the-hood tweaks, it introduces a major transparency upgrade for how the OS handles sensitive on-device data. The new release adds a dedicated “Data logging” section for the Private Compute Core right inside Privacy Dashboard. Private Compute Core is Android’s isolated sandbox that powers machine learning features such as Live Caption, Now Playing, and Smart Reply, without exposing user data directly to the cloud or other apps. While Private Compute Core has historically operated in a secure silo, this new Privacy Dashboard entry in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 lets users actively monitor, log, and review any outbound data leaving the Private Compute Core environment.

title: Survey reveals your favorite Pixel 11 Pro XL alternatives
summary: Our readers' top Pixel 11 Pro XL alternative may not be what you think it is
body: Sometimes, upgrading to the latest smartphone is a simple process. A lot of us look at the phone we have now, and if we liked it, we look for the newest version of the same thing: probably more powerful, likely introducing a couple new features, and hopefully not costing too much more. But the market doesn’t always make things so simple for us, and this year with Google’s new Pixel 11 series, some shoppers might want to take a long, hard look at exactly what those upgrades offer — and what Google wants us to pay for them. A little over a week ago, we asked you to really break things down for us. This year’s Pixel 11 Pro phones can feel a little underwhelming depending on your expectations, but what are shoppers supposed to do about it? Well, the playing field in 2026 is sure a whole lot smaller than it’s been in years past, but that doesn’t mean there aren’t some solid options out there. And honestly, between lengthy software update guarantees and all the craziness happening now with RAM values in light of the market losing its mind, maybe it really does make sense to go with something other than the very, very latest phone.

The update also brings new icons, YouTube Music improvements, and several playback fixes across Free and Premium versions. The developer is already working on phone-to-car YouTube playback and a proper EPG guide, with another update expected this weekend. Waiting in a parked car while someone runs into a shop is hardly the most exciting way to spend a few minutes. That familiar scenario apparently gave the developer behind Android Auto app Xtream Player an idea: why not put a few simple games on the dashboard for those moments when the car isn’t moving? That idea is now part of Xtream Player v1.4.0, which also brings new icons, YouTube Music improvements, and playback fixes. Xtream Player is the successor to Fermata Xtream, which became popular among Android Auto enthusiasts for bringing video playback and other unofficial features to compatible car displays. The developer had previously announced that Fermata Xtream was being sunset, only to return with a completely rewritten app. The latest version 1.4.0 now gives that project another significant upgrade.

title: Google Messages has a bizarre bug that’s sending old texts to random people
summary: Old conversations are allegedly resurfacing in places they definitely shouldn’t.
body: TL;DR Some Google Messages users say old texts from unrelated conversations are unexpectedly resurfacing. Reports span multiple Pixel and Samsung phones. In some cases, those messages appear to be sent alongside new texts or images, raising serious privacy concerns. Google Messages is getting some welcome attention with custom chat themes and selective text copying finally becoming available, but the app’s recent run of bugs is taking some shine off those additions. Besides broken RCS messaging and conversations turning into multiple threads , users are reporting a more worrying problem: Messages appears to be pulling old texts from unrelated conversations and attaching or sending them with new messages. Several Reddit reports describe the same basic nightmare. A user starts a new conversation, only for Messages to insert a message from a completely different chat, sometimes from months or even years ago. In some cases, the stray text appears alongside a photo or group message. In others, users say the old message actually reaches the unintended recipient.

title: I lived with Samsung’s worst 2025 Android phone for a year. Here’s why I’m finally giving up

body: Three months after Samsung launched the three mainline Galaxy S25 models, it followed up with a fourth offering: the Galaxy S25 Edge. By all indications, Samsung released the ultra-thin Galaxy S25 Edge to get ahead of the iPhone Air, and it almost worked. The Galaxy S25 Edge came with better specs and fewer compromises than the iPhone Air, but one year later, Samsung’s slim flagship has no successor in sight. It’s easily the brand’s worst phone of 2025, and seems destined to be forgotten as a quirky flop. I bought the Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge in cash, with no promotions or discounts, and used it for the last year. Whenever I wasn’t reviewing a new Android phone, the Galaxy S25 Edge was my daily driver. I still love the concept, but I struggled to live with Samsung’s execution.

body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4, which was released last week, brings an easier way to broadcast your voice over a private network. The new Audio broadcast feature expands Pixels’ existing Auracast-based media-sharing features to transmit audio over Bluetooth LE Audio. While the feature was introduced last month, it is now much easier to access. Google is in the final legs of testing Android 17 QPR2 Beta before a significant feature drop for Pixels in September. Last Friday, it released the fourth QPR2 Beta, sorting out a long list of bugs and usability issues from previous beta builds. As part of Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 , Google is adding a few useful features that didn’t make it into the changelog, including easier access to Voice Broadcast. Voice Broadcast on Pixel devices with Android 17 QPR2 Beta is like a personal PA system. It lets users voice their views over, or share audio from a media player, in private listening channels. This private network is enabled by Bluetooth LE (Low Energy), and audio devices — earbuds and such — used by recipients must support the technology.

title: Lake Ontario is now ‘Lake America’ on Google Maps, but not for everyone

body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google Maps is now starting to call Lake Ontario “Lake America” following recent executive orders. Last week, President Trump signed the executive order to rename the lake officially. Google says the new change is only visible for people in the US, while those in Canada will continue to see “Lake Ontario.” Last week, US President Donald Trump signed executive orders to officially rename Lake Ontario “Lake America,” his second re-christening, so to speak, of a body of water after the Gulf of Mexico . Following these official orders, Google Maps has started showing the name of the body of water bordering both the US and Canada. In an official announcement , Google noted it will start showing the lake’s new official name, as designated by the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS). It said the official name change will appear on Google Maps, but only for people in the US.

summary: The glow-up isn't finished yet.
body: I miss the days when notification LEDs were a thing. I still remember the red light flashing on my BlackBerry whenever a notification came in. I’d immediately pick up my phone and check what I’d missed. Smartphones have mostly left that idea behind. Yes, Nothing did bring it back in its own way with the Glyph lights, but personally, that feels like a little too much of a light show. That’s why Google’s HiLight feature on the Pixel 11 Pro series immediately caught my attention. It feels like a much more modern take on the notification LED I used to love. The light sits neatly inside the camera visor; it can glow in different colors, and it’s quite subtle. But the problem is, after using HiLight, I can’t stop thinking about how much more useful it could be .

title: Spotify could soon let you host a Jam without Premium
summary: With strings attached, of course.
body: TL;DR Spotify could soon let Free users host their own collaborative Jams, removing the current Premium-only requirement. Jams hosted by Free users may force shuffle, limit skips, and cap the queue for everyone, including Premium participants. App strings in Spotify 9.1.82.19 hint at the change, but there’s no guarantee the feature will actually roll out. Spotify released Jam, a fully collaborative real-time playlist that can be joined by up to 32 individuals, back in September of 2023. It’s one of Spotify’s best features , and it’s turning three next month. To celebrate the occasion, the music streaming giant might finally be ready to make hosting Jams a lot more accessible. For reference, joining and participating in Jams is available to all, but hosting one requires you to be a Spotify Premium subscriber. Essentially, joining someone’s party is a free affair, but if you want to host a party, you’ll have to open up your wallet. That caveat, however, could soon disappear.
